requests.note: the whole of device authentication: one static tenant key in the Authorization header, and the box's MAC in the body. No timestamp, no nonce, no signature, no canonical string — an unknown or missing key is a plain 401 and an unknown MAC auto-registers a device.
device-authenticated activation: a pre-booked member's code, resolved to their booking on one of this box's courts. `mac` is how the request names the device.

six-field walk-up: court is the court NUMBER the member selected, nonce is the box's 16-hex purchase nonce that makes a retry replay-safe. The nonce is idempotency, not authentication — it survived the removal of request signing for that reason.

the 49.7-day millis() wrap on the events path (review 3, finding 25): the batch uptime and the queued event's uptime are both past 2^32, so a firmware that renders either through a 32-bit conversion uploads a different number than this.

`restored_relays` is how many relays this box re-energised from the last served restore. It is how the server learns the restore LANDED: a served restore followed by a zero — or by an absent field, which reads as zero — is the row an admin must see, because it means a court is dark that should not be. Omitted at zero, so a board with nothing to report sends the `heartbeat-request` body above, byte for byte.

`relay_state` is what the box BELIEVES is closed, carried up from the Mega's !STATE, so the control board can say 'lights on — confirmed by the box' instead of only what it granted. Same pipe-delimited string array as the restore, for the same heapless-scanner reason, as <relay>|<remaining_seconds>. THREE STATES, NOT TWO: the key ABSENT means this firmware does not report relay state, an EMPTY ARRAY means the box believes nothing is closed. Both new fields must bind as nullable 64-bit on the server — an out-of-range value must not 400 the whole heartbeat, which is why no_push and events_lost are long? and not int?.

The COURT BOX's event body carrying a real `boot_id` — the third field of the idempotency key (round G4, C2). The court box hardcodes 0 today, which omits the field; the server reads an absent boot_id as 0, which is exactly what (device, seq) always meant, so this vector is the change and not the status quo. Without it, a torn or erased seq checkpoint renumbers the board from 1 and every event of the next evening is receipted as a duplicate and discarded — including the `boot` event queued so an operator can see the board restarted. Position is part of the shape: immediately after `mac`, before `uptime_ms`.

R15 D15-1: the Mega passes every scanner byte through, quotes, backslashes and bytes above 0x7F included, and the bridge interpolated the token raw — invalid JSON (the quote ended the string) and invalid UTF-8 (a lone 0xE9). `token_hex` is the scan as it came off the serial link: Q " \ X 0xE9 0xFF. The body escapes it with devapi::json::escapeInto: the two-character forms for the quote and the backslash, and every byte above 0x7E as \u00XX, its Latin-1 code point, so the body is pure ASCII, valid JSON and valid UTF-8 whatever was scanned. Not a v1 member code, so no scan_age_ms. The server reads the token as the string Q"\Xéÿ and refuses it like any unknown code.
the same scan as activate-request-escaped-scan, in the walk-up body (60 minutes on court 3): the token is escaped exactly as it is there.

the same scan, refused offline and queued as an unknown_scan: its subject was already escaped for the quote and the backslash (round G4, B1) but carried 0xE9 raw, and the server answered that body 500 — the drain retried it for ever and the breaker read it as an outage. `subject_hex` is the queued subject. Boot id 0, so the field is omitted.

bridge 2.3.0: extending a LIT court at the panel. Same wire as the walk-up (device auth, the box's MAC, the member's scanned token, the club court NUMBER, a 16-hex nonce reused only on a retry of the same undecided extension) in the order bridgelogic::renderExtendBody writes it: mac, method, token, court, minutes, nonce. Thirty minutes on court 3. A v1 member code would add scan_age_ms exactly as the walk-up does.

heartbeat v3 (docs/specs/device-api.md). A bridge 3.x box on a quiet beat. Field order is the renderer's: the 2.x fields, then mega_version, net_ver, net_src, lcd_layout, then caps LAST. `caps` names every v3 capability the image has; the server keys every new response field on them, so a 2.x box (caps codes:m1 at most) is answered exactly as today.

The first beat after a bridge boot, before the Mega's first !STATE of this boot has arrived: relay_state is ABSENT (not reported), never an empty array, which the server would read as 'confirmed off' for every relay (BR-12). mega_version absent too: not yet heard. restore warm: this boot was not a power-on, so the bridge re-lit from an RTC-dated snapshot (cold = a power-on reset used the flash snapshot inside device_power_restore_trust_minutes; none = nothing to restore). Sent on the first accepted beat of a boot only.

relight names every relay the bridge re-lit FROM THE SNAPSHOT since the last accepted beat, as <relay>|<ref>: how the server learns a reconcile landed (it replaces restored_relays, which a v3 box never sends). Here relay 0 after a Mega-only reset. net_src local: the network was set at the box's setup portal, so the server does not push its own over it.

heartbeat v3 (docs/specs/device-api.md). A release now says WHY the relay opened. `cause` is member (the OFF button), autooff (the Mega's own deadline), cap (the Mega's authorisation cap), mega_reset (the Mega rebooted and opened every relay) or reconcile (the box cancelled its own provisional power-restore light). Only a member release paired with the session takes the booking out of the snapshot; a mega_reset release never does (BD-2). Absent means member: every 2.x box.

Telemetry a frozen board must report because nothing else will ever tell the club (device-api.md section 13), after lcd_layout and before caps: `mega` (from the Mega's !BOOT, !HW and !DIAG of its current boot: MCUSR, the LCD address that answered or 00, the effective relay level, scanner baud (0 while auto has not locked) and line end, the unarmed-forward key mask, the five since-boot counters) and `diag` (the bridge's own: reset reason, exception cause and epc1, free heap now and lowest since boot, largest free block, lowest free continuation stack since boot, free sketch space, real flash size in MB). Every number is a JSON integer; `mega` is absent until the Mega has been heard this Mega boot.
The widest request a 3.0.0 bridge can render: every field at its bound, eight drift names. It must fit the bridge's 1536-byte render buffer (compat/ budgets) and the server must accept it.

responses.note: granted_seconds is what the box puts on the relay timer: EndsAt-now clamped to the relay hard cap, so a 45-minute remainder is 2700
inside the forward window but outside the cue window: identified, not stamped, nothing on the relay; the box shows starts_in_seconds
the same (device, nonce) seen again: the original grant comes back with replayed:true so a box that lost the first 200 can still !ON, and nobody is charged twice
one physical box drives up to four relays (review C4): court_numbers is the relay mapping, index 0 = relay A; an empty roster is a box with nothing booked in the window, not a missing key

the roster push (review C2): TOKEN|relay|opens_in|closes_in — relay is the index into court_numbers, opens_in is SIGNED seconds until StartsAt minus the cue window (negative = already open), closes_in is seconds until EndsAt
RosterMaxEntries = 16 is a contract constant bounding the firmware buffer, not a tenant setting; entries are ordered by StartsAt and the whole body must fit the box's 2048-byte response buffer
a booking that started 30 minutes ago with 15 left: opens_in is negative and the box clamps it to 'open now'; closes_in still counts down from the response instant

a replay grants the REMAINDER of the purchase from now, never the original length: the same nonce forty minutes after a lost 60-minute grant answers granted_minutes:25 (rounded up), and a purchase whose window has ended is 409 purchase_ended rather than a grant at all (closing re-review #20)

a scan inside the grace window after the slot ended is stamped as attendance but there is nothing left to light: activated:false with reason ended and granted_seconds 0, never activated:true with zero seconds, which the box turned into a one-second relay pulse and a spent scan

GOAL 17, the power-dip restore. `relays` is what SHOULD BE ON, as <relay>|<remaining_seconds>|<booking_ref> — pipe-delimited strings and not objects, because the firmware has a heapless JSON scanner and no object-array walker. remaining_seconds is the UNCAPPED true remainder relative to the instant this response was produced, exactly like the roster's opens_in/closes_in, which is what makes the restore usable on a box that has just lost power and does not know what time it is. Parsed to (0, 1834) and (2, 600); booking_ref is the booking id's first eight hex, for the trace, and is NEVER the activation code.

`relays` present and empty: nothing should be on. It restores nothing AND SWITCHES NOTHING OFF — making an empty array an off-command would hand the API a way to darken a court mid-game, and a dropped response would do it by accident. Different from the absent key below: this says the server has an opinion and the opinion is none.

No `relays` key at all: this API does not do restore. The box must not wait for one and must not restore anything — and must not read the absence as 'switch everything off'. This is the body every court box in the field is answered with today, so it is also the compatibility case.

Two bad elements and one good one. `9|100|x` names a relay this box does not have and `0|abc|y` has non-numeric seconds; both are SKIPPED AND COUNTED, and `1|500|z` is still applied. One bad element must not cost the well-formed ones — the roster's rule, with a court that is dark and should not be as the cost. A two-digit relay is malformed too, not relay 1: a relay number is an index, not a quantity.

remaining_seconds of 9999 is nearly three hours, well past the 5400 s relay hard cap. It comes through UNCAPPED: the box clamps the !ON to ninety minutes itself, twice, and arms its !EXT extension logic from the uncapped value. Capping it on the wire would hide from the bridge that the booking outlives the relay deadline, and the court would go dark ninety minutes in with half the booking left.

All nine operator settings inside the nested `config`, at non-default values inside every bound: each is adopted and each is clamped. They are read ONE LEVEL DEEP from the top-level `config` and nowhere else — devapi's flat scan takes the first match in document order, so a vendor or diagnostics block nesting the same names would otherwise drive the screen. The cross-key invariant scan_memory_seconds >= lcd_choice_seconds holds here (200 >= 45) and is enforced by RAISING the memory, never by lowering the choice window.

Every one of the seven numeric settings outside its bound, in BOTH directions across the set — a single value cannot be past two bounds at once, so revert/card/clock_trust/fault_max are past their ceilings and choice/hint/scan_memory are past their floors. Each is CLAMPED and none refuses the eight beside it: a club that typed 3600 into one field must not thereby lose its button map. Note that scan_memory_seconds of 2 is raised to the clamped lcd_choice_seconds of 5 rather than lcd_choice_seconds being lowered to 2.

`member_display` is the member's name for the LCD's greeting line, appended after granted_seconds so it is purely additive. THE BACKEND DOES NOT EMIT THIS FIELD YET — this vector declares the contract the server must then satisfy, which is the direction this corpus is allowed to run in.

No `member_display`: the box greets with HI THERE. An absent name is the ordinary case for a club that has not filled the field in, and an unnamed member must still get their court — so absence changes the greeting and nothing else. granted_seconds differs from activate-response-ok-named so the two vectors are not byte-identical.

A forty-character `member_display`. devapi::json::stringField REFUSES rather than truncates when a value will not fit the caller's buffer — half a value is a different value — so the box shows HI THERE and NEVER a truncated name. The refusal is a property of the box's buffer, which is sized to the LCD's twenty columns; the wire itself carries whatever the server sent, which is why the server must cap the field rather than relying on the board to.

a granted extension: extended_minutes is what the server ACTUALLY added (truncated before the next booking) and is what the relay is given, never what was asked; balance_after_minutes is the member's balance after the charge and reads BALANCE <n> MIN on the glass. greeting_name rides along and the box does not need it here.

the server could only sell twenty of the sixty minutes asked before the next booking: the relay gets twenty and the glass says +20. No balance_after_minutes (an older server): the box reads ENJOY YOUR GAME instead of a balance it was not told.
nothing is in play on that court any more (it went dark between the press and the request): COURT NOT ON / PICK ANOTHER, decided, nonce spent, scan kept.
the next booking starts at the session's end: NO TIME BEFORE / NEXT BOOKING.
the scanning member's balance cannot pay for the extension: TOO FEW MINUTES / BUY & RETRY.

bridge 2.3.0's greeting: greeting_name and balance_minutes are read TOLERANTLY (either may be absent) and greet a recognised scan with HI <NAME> / BALANCE <n> MIN before the outcome. The server sends the member's first name ASCII-folded and upper-cased (MemberDisplay.GreetingNameAsync, at most sixteen characters); the box keeps printable ASCII only, upper-cases it again, cut to thirteen columns on the glass (HI plus thirteen is the 1602's sixteen). Additive: an older backend that sends neither greets HI / WELCOME.

heartbeat v3 (docs/specs/device-api.md). The complete snapshot, every beat, for an ACKNOWLEDGED box with caps hb:3: `courts` has one element per mapped relay in relay order, <relay>|<lit>|<seconds_left>|<kind>|<ref>. seconds_left is the UNCAPPED paid remainder to the end of the chained run (extensions included), relative to this response; kind b booking, w walk-up, e an extension is in play, '-' dark; ref the first eight hex of the booking in play. Dark relays are listed too: the snapshot is complete, never a delta. The box re-lights from it (never switches anything off) when relay_restore_enabled, and always uses it for the landing's minutes. The thirteen v3 config keys follow the twelve 2.x ones inside `config`.

A box no admin has acknowledged gets NO `courts` key: no snapshot, so no re-light and no restore — an auto-registered board's court map is a guess until a person confirms it (BR-13). Absent is 'no opinion', never 'everything dark'.
This board is overridden to the expanded layout with the marquee off; every other v3 key at a non-default value inside its bound.

Every v3 number past its bound and an unknown layout: each is CLAMPED independently and none costs its neighbours, and a layout the box does not know is COMPACT — the safe one, which reads whole on both panels.

A key rotation in its grace window: the box persists key_next, authenticates the NEXT request with it, and keeps its previous key as the fallback for a 401. Present until the server has seen this board authenticate with k2.

A network change: sent only to a box whose reported net_ver is lower and whose net_src is not local. Adoption is all-or-nothing (provision/cases.json nets); the box keeps the previous set as its fallback and reverts the base URL if no heartbeat is accepted within device_net_fallback_minutes.

The widest body the v3 contract allows a court box, run through the server's Fit: heartbeat-response-codes-full's 2 days and 64-character slug, its roster widened to 16 legacy entries at the 20-character token bound and six-digit seconds, every v3 display and hardware config key at its widest, four widest snapshot elements, a key rotation and a two-profile network at their bounds, and then the member-code keys, which the server sheds first and lowest priority last when a body is over budget — here all 64 a v3 ring holds fit, so none is shed. 3984 bytes against the v3 contract of 4096; a v3 bridge reads into a 5120-byte buffer. A key and a network are each transient, so the server never really sends both at once. A 2.x box is never sent any of this and keeps its 2048-byte contract.

play_remaining_seconds is the UNCAPPED time to the end of the chained run of checked-in bookings on this court, beside granted_seconds (capped at 5400 for the relay). A 105-minute booking activated online used to go dark at minute 90 because the bridge fed the capped value to Relight (FSF-05); a v3 bridge arms Relight from this field and falls back to granted_seconds when it is absent (every 2.x server).

The hardware facts a frozen Mega can no longer have compiled in (device-api.md section 12): this board's relays are low-trigger, its LCD backpack answers at 0x3F (63), its scanner runs at 9600 with a CR/LF suffix and a 100 ms gap. Each is a tenant setting with a per-board override, sent in `config` after the thirteen v3 display keys and before button_map, and passed to the Mega as !CFG RPOL, LCDA, SBAUD, SSUF and SGAP. An unknown value keeps the current one; a wrong relay level fails DARK, never lit, because the Mega releases a relay by making its pin an input.

The lifeline-only answer (device-api.md section 11): what the server sends on alternate beats if the rest of a body could ever not fit its budget even with every code key dropped. No court_numbers, config, courts or roster: absent is 'no opinion', so the box keeps all of them, and adopts the key rotation and the network change. With today's fields it never fires; it exists so that no future field can starve the two paths that keep a board reachable.
